:::{#def-data-splits}
#### Training/validation/test split

A **training/validation/test split** divides the observations $1, \ldots, n$
into three disjoint sets of indices:
$I_{\text{train}}$ for the [training set](#def-training-set),
$I_{\text{val}}$ for the [validation set](#def-validation-set),
and $I_{\text{test}}$ for the [test set](#def-test-set):

$$
I_{\text{train}} \cup I_{\text{val}} \cup I_{\text{test}} = \set{1, \ldots, n}.
$$ {#eq-data-splits}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
#### Source

Adapted from the rme notes' section [Train/validation/test splits](https://morrison-lab.github.io/rme/chapters/Linear-models-overview.html#trainvalidationtest-splits),
which follows @james2021islr2e [pp. 198--201].
:::

:::

::: notes
This validation approach extends the basic train/test split
by separating model tuning
from final model assessment.
It follows @james2021islr2e [pp. 198-201].

Keeping the test set untouched during model building
helps avoid optimistic bias
from repeatedly trying many models.
In @exr-data-splits,
a rule of 60% / 20% / 20% on $n = 32$ cars
gives sets of 19, 6, and 7 cars,
and the 7 test cars are used only once, after the model is chosen.
:::
